The lamp shown in the diagram below can move along the vertical line $OB$ using a pulley system. The point $A$ lies on the horizontal line $OA$ at a distance of $d$ from $O$. The intensity $I$ of light from the lamp at point $A$ is inversely proportional to the square of its distance $r$ from the lamp. The intensity $I$ is also directly proportional to $\sin\phi$, where $\phi$ is the angle of elevation from $A$ to the lamp. Hence, the formula for $I$ can be expressed as:
$$I=\dfrac{C\sin\phi}{r^2}, \quad \text{where } C \text{ is a positive constant.}$$
